withdraw.missing: An observable road-user class for the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab ('a motor vehicle which is properly licensed under State and local law to provide taxicab service for a charge or fee') that the run's reading can classify as included. Right now the reading lists no included class under that id and marks ru.taxicab as unresolved. So ru.aggregate=DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab can never be true: it is unknown for every taxicab and false for everything else. The s1 binder class, and the same aggregate on s5, therefore never let the duty be judged. The span decides which road users the duty concerns: the taxicab whose standing outside a taxicab stand is forbidden. One of two things is needed. Either a class atom whose contract carries the licence to provide taxicab service, or an operator decision that this licensing status is read through the taxicab's markings (an observable_reading of category status, under which ru.taxicab is classified as included in DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab). In both cases the rule, mappings and witnesses written for this node need no further change.
nearest: ru.taxicab: 'passenger vehicle for hire, identifiable by its markings'. The run's reading classifies it as unresolved under DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab, because its markings are not shown to be the licence 'under State and local law' that the definition requires

ru.aggregate: 'true when the user carries an included class, unknown when no included class holds and the user carries an unresolved class ...; an admitted aggregate stays an aggregate even when it contains only one class'. With no included class it is never true, and the term may not be re-mapped to ru.taxicab's own class atom
